title: NASA Watched Ice Near the Equator Melt. Only 2% Is Left.
description:
The Puncak Jaya glacier in New Guinea is one of the last places near the equator with ice. NASA Landsat images from 1988 and 2026 show it has shrunk to about 2% of its 1988 area, and scientists say the last ice could be gone within a few years.

Key numbers (NASA Earth Observatory, Nov 16, 2026, citing Donaldi Permana, BMKG): about 4.31 km² (1.66 sq mi) of ice in 1988; about 0.09 km² by September 2025, roughly 2% of the 1988 extent. Ice at the East Northwall Firn site thinned from 32 m (105 ft) in 2010 to 4 m (13 ft) in 2023 and was gone by November 2024.
